audit_findings.title: Anchor does not reflect a full year of the refinanced debt’s higher interest cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.911 million pre-tax annualized interest adjustment; approximately $9.076 million after tax, $120.7 million of base value, or $3.28 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE anchor retains interest expense, so the post-refinancing recurring interest cost must be reflected in OE rather than through a debt deduction in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On November 13, 2025, TWCC issued $575.0 million principal amount of senior notes at par, bearing interest at a rate of 7.375% per annum, and maturing on February 15, 2031.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated normalization error if the $100.4 million anchor uses fiscal 2025 without adjustment. Fiscal 2025 interest expense was $34.227 million, while the first two fiscal quarters of 2026 incurred $23.069 million, implying a $46.138 million annual run rate and an $11.911 million pre-tax increase. Using the filed 23.8% interim tax rate and the base operating-PV-to-anchor ratio, the correction would reduce base value by about $3.28 per share and the 30%-MOS buy-below price from $37.78 to about $35.48. That remains above the $33.55 market price, so this finding alone does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate normalized annual interest using the note coupon, issuance-cost amortization, ABL fees, and removal of fiscal 2025 overlap costs; rerun OE and confirm the buy-below result.

audit_findings.title: The bridge treats the entire cash balance as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $653.571 million, equal to $17.74 per diluted share and 32.9% of the $1.988 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash dollar-for-dollar to equity value even though operating or committed cash is already required to support inventory, payroll, interest, taxes, capital expenditures, and seasonal working capital.
audit_findings.evidence: Our ongoing cash needs are primarily for working capital (consisting primarily of inventory), capital expenditures, employee compensation, interest on debt, the return of capital to our shareholders, and other general corporate purposes.
audit_findings.explanation: The full cash addition is demonstrated, but the amount that is genuinely excess remains unresolved. Its scale is material: treating only $222.5 million of the balance as unavailable would reduce base value enough to move the 30%-MOS buy-below level from $37.78 to the $33.55 market price. The filing identifies substantial seasonal and inventory funding needs, and $27.030 million of income taxes payable included taxes arising from the tariff refund, so assuming every dollar is distributable is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build a quarterly cash bridge covering seasonal lows, inventory and payable cycles, restricted accounts, the tariff-refund tax payment, interest, capital spending, dividends, and other committed payments; rerun the valuation using only demonstrated excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains an extra operating week that the forecast may perpetuate
audit_findings.magnitude: $37 million incremental sales; approximately $16.8 million gross profit before related expenses and approximately $12.8 million after tax using the filed 45.4% gross margin and 23.8% tax rate
audit_findings.mechanism: If the 53rd week's earnings and working-capital effects remain in anchor OE, the DCF applies scenario growth and terminal value to nonrecurring annual activity.
audit_findings.evidence: The 53rd week in fiscal 2025 contributed approximately $37 million of incremental consolidated net sales.
audit_findings.explanation: The extra week and its $37 million of sales are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the $100.4 million anchor was normalized or quantify the week's net OE contribution. The computed gross-profit proxy could reduce base value by roughly $170 million, or $4.62 per share, before accounting for variable SG&A and working-capital effects. That proxy alone would leave the buy-below level near $34.55, but the unreported working-capital effect prevents a reliable materiality conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Extract the 53rd week's gross profit, variable SG&A, taxes, receivables, inventory, and payables from the ledger; remove its complete OE contribution and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Tariff-loaded inventory may distort the latest owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $110 million of fiscal 2025 tariffs paid, $60 million recognized in product costs, $50 million capitalized in inventory; subsequently $132 million of IEEPA refunds including $128 million recorded against cost of goods sold and $4 million of interest
audit_findings.mechanism: Tariff cash payments affect working capital and OE before inventory is sold, product costs affect earnings later, and refunds may enter either OE or the cash bridge; inconsistent treatment can omit or double-count the same economics.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 3, 2026, approximately $50 million of incremental tariff costs were capitalized within our inventory balances.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated and its components are large relative to the $100.4 million anchor. The direction cannot be fixed from the record: an abnormal inventory cash outflow can depress OE and understate value, while inclusion of the later $128 million cost recovery or $4 million refund interest as recurring OE can overstate value. Because the July cash bridge also captures refund proceeds, normalization without a complete rollforward could double-count recovery. The amounts are plainly capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile by tariff regime and inventory cohort the $110 million paid, $60 million expensed, $50 million capitalized, subsequent Section 122 tariffs, inventory sold, $132 million received, related taxes, and remaining claims; then rerun OE with one-time refunds excluded from recurring earnings and counted only once in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Restricted Rabbi Trust assets must not be added without the deferred-compensation claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 included in the bridge; $23.0 million of Rabbi Trust assets were classified in prepaid expenses and other current assets rather than cash
audit_findings.mechanism: A bridge error would arise only if restricted trust investments were included as excess cash without the matching deferred-compensation liability.
audit_findings.evidence: The Rabbi Trust investments are restricted in their use to meet funding obligations to Plan participants.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied filings resolve the conditional concern. The $653.571 million bridge amount exactly matches reported cash and cash equivalents, while the $23.0 million Rabbi Trust investments were separately reported in prepaid expenses and other current assets and backed deferred-compensation obligations in other current liabilities. Therefore none of the trust assets entered the bridge, producing no effect on the $1.988 billion base equity value.
audit_findings.action: Retain the present balance-sheet mapping and verify in future reruns that neither Rabbi Trust assets nor their matching liability are reclassified into excess cash.
